title: Benue Government and CRS Launch RAPID Humanitarian Project
summary: A 12-month humanitarian initiative announced by the Benue State Government and Catholic Relief Services will cover 19 communities across four local government areas, including Agatu.
content:
The Benue State Government, in partnership with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) and other stakeholders, announced the Rapid Assistance for People Impacted by Disaster (RAPID) project in October 2026.

The state government's announcement says the 12-month initiative covers 19 communities across Gwer West, Agatu, Kwande and Logo local government areas. Planned intervention areas include food assistance, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, shelter, protection, disaster-risk reduction and community engagement.

The announcement describes the project's intended scope. It does not confirm that every service has already reached Agatu communities. Residents should look for further implementation updates from the responsible agencies.

Source: Benue State Ministry of Information and Orientation. Published October 22, 2026.
author: Agatu LGA News Desk

title: Agatu Council Awards Contracts for Three Asphalt Roads
summary: A September report described contracts for the Oshigbudu–Atakpa, Market Square–Onchali and Adokpa–Och’Adogoji roads.
content:
A report published on September 18, 2026, said the Agatu Local Government Council had awarded contracts to RCSY Construction Nigeria Limited for three asphalt road projects.

  • Oshigbudu–Atakpa Road
  • Market Square–Onchali Road
  • Adokpa–Och’Adogoji Road

The report said work was expected to commence in the fourth week of September. This article records the reported contract awards; it does not confirm that construction has started, reached a particular stage or been completed. A newer, independently verified progress update is needed to establish the current status.

Source: Benue Today. Published September 18, 2026.

title: State Team Inspects School Renovations and Road Project in Agatu
summary: A July report described an inspection of classroom renovation work at RCM Primary School in Oweto and Ogbaulu and the Obagaji–Okokolo–Agagbe Road project.
content:
According to a report published on July 1, 2026, a Benue State Government monitoring team inspected projects in Agatu on June 30.

The reported inspection covered classroom renovation work at RCM Primary School in Oweto and Ogbaulu, as well as the Obagaji–Okokolo–Agagbe Road project.

The report documents an inspection at that time. It does not establish whether the works have since been completed or their current construction status.

Source: Benue Today. Published July 1, 2026.

title: Apa–Agatu Town Hall Highlights Development Priorities
summary: Reporting on the August town hall meeting covered development priorities, including infrastructure and agricultural development.
content:
Reports published on August 29, 2026, covered a town hall meeting involving the Benue State Government and stakeholders from the Apa–Agatu area. Topics included infrastructure and broader development priorities.

This article summarizes the reported meeting and the priorities discussed. Statements made at a town hall should be understood as attributed statements or commitments, not independent confirmation that every proposed project has been completed.

Sources: Benue Today and Daily Post. Published August 29, 2026.

title: Agatu Chairman Leads SEMA, IOM and Red Cross in Assessment of 32 Flood-Affected Communities
summary: Agatu LGA Chairman Hon. Amb. James Melvin Ejeh appeals for urgent humanitarian assistance following a joint assessment of 32 flood-affected communities, alongside the distribution of 150 life jackets supplied by HYPPADEC.
content:
The Executive Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area, Hon. Amb. James Melvin Ejeh, has appealed for urgent humanitarian assistance for 32 communities reportedly affected by flooding. The appeal was made on Sunday, October 18, 2026, when the Chairman received a joint rapid assessment team from the Benue State Emergency Management Agency (Benue-SEMA), the International Organization for Migration (IOM), and the Nigerian Red Cross.

The team visited to assess the impact of the flooding, identify urgent needs, and help guide possible humanitarian interventions. The Chairman received the delegation alongside the community leaders of Oweto and Utugolugu, Chief Ibrahim Kwelono and Chief Sule Ajaka.

Reports indicated that houses, farmlands, food supplies, and household items had been damaged. These losses have raised concerns about shelter, food security, and the livelihoods of affected residents.

As part of efforts to improve water safety, the Chairman distributed 150 life jackets supplied by HYPPADEC to major boat points, including Oweto, Adana, Abugbe, and other locations. He commended HYPPADEC for its support and urged boat operators and passengers to obey water-safety rules and wear life jackets while travelling by water.

The Chairman appealed to the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Benue-SEMA, relevant government agencies, humanitarian organisations, and development partners to provide urgent assistance. Priority needs include relief supplies, food, shelter, medical assistance, and livelihood support for affected households.

He was accompanied by nine ward councillors led by the Agatu Legislative Council Leader, Hon. Tony Simon, as well as the Supervisory Councillor for Revenue, Hon. Danjuma Isah Halidu, and other council officials.

The assessment was coordinated by the Executive Secretary of Benue-SEMA, Sir James Aondoakaa Iorpuu, PhD. The team was led by Mr. Orseer Zege, Programme Manager for IDP Operations, who represented the Executive Secretary alongside representatives of IOM and the Nigerian Red Cross.

Mr. Zege expressed sympathy with the affected communities and explained that the assessment findings would help establish the extent of the damage and guide intervention efforts. He added that Benue-SEMA was working with relevant agencies and development partners to facilitate assistance.

The visit highlighted the urgent needs of flood-affected riverine communities and the importance of coordinated humanitarian support, community cooperation, and safe water transportation.
author: Agatu LGA Media Office
